If feasible, integrate unmodified elastic direct-NVLink DeepEP while holding Marlin, routing semantics, payload format, topology, and speculation fixed. hypotheses.statement: Test direct-NVLink DeepEP dispatch in two attributable stages: compatible backend activation, followed by the triple-buffered prefetch change in #693. First verify the effective baseline transport, four-rank NVLink connectivity, and whether the pinned engine can reach the elastic direct-NVLink implementation while preserving Marlin and its activation payload. The supplied patch overlaps preparation of the next token with outstanding remote stores, but its positive evidence is an eight-H100, remote-only bandwidth test. Four-rank serving may have more local traffic, smaller messages, and greater resource contention. Compare unmodified DeepEP with the baseline before comparing patched and unmodified DeepEP at fixed compute and numeric settings. Resolve the buffer-lifetime invariant and graph behavior before performance testing. Historical mixed-configuration regressions motivate these controls but do not establish that DeepEP will lose here.
